title: Don’t Start an Airbnb Arbitrage business before watching this
summary: Arbitrage operator explains lease addendums, negotiating free rent and small deposits, choosing landlords and cheaper units; claims anyone disciplined can build a six- or seven-figure business.

assertions.quote: You just need the landlord's permission.

verdicts.note: Subletting without consent breaches most leases, and many cities license or ban short-term rentals.

assertions.quote: You're not going to make more money because you paid more rent. You're still going to collect the same amount of cash.

verdicts.note: Booking revenue is set by the market, so rent is a direct subtraction from margin.

assertions.quote: if you can spend the same amount of money for furniture but then get two years of revenue off of that lease, it's much better

verdicts.note: Furniture is a fixed setup cost amortized over the lease term.

assertions.quote: it costs about 1/8 of the price to set up an Airbnb as an arbitrage as opposed to buying
There's people exiting the industry right now. And as suppliers leave the industry and guests stay in the industry, there'll be less suppliers

verdicts.note: Supply exits can help, but downturns also cut travel demand and nightly rates.
Supply exits can lower competition and furniture costs, but downturns also cut travel demand and nightly rates.

assertions.quote: It's a pretty easy industry. I think anybody can.

verdicts.note: Market saturation, regulation and landlord refusals mean most entrants do not reach those revenues.

assertions.quote: the landlord can and will give you permission if you present yourself the right way
